items.title: Will Germany scrap its early retirement scheme?
items.summary: Germany is working on a major pension reform, with plans to scrap the 'Rente mit 63' early retirement scheme. What is it and why is it being targeted?
items.body_text:
If you've spent any time in Germany in the last few years, you've probably heard that a demographic timebomb is ticking.
As people live longer and the birth rate falls, Germany – like much of Europe and many other countries – faces a serious challenge to keep the labour market booming and the social security system afloat.
A huge overhaul of the pension system is on the cards, with a commission recommending raising the retirement age and expanding compulsory pension contributions to include civil servants and self-employed workers.
As part of the proposals, an early retirement option called "Rente mit 63" (or pension at 63) would be scrapped.
What is Rente mit 63?
The standard retirement age in Germany is currently 66 years and six months, and is being gradually increased to 67. But in some cases people can retire and receive their pension earlier.
It all depends on a person's age and how many qualifying years they have accumulated in the pension insurance system (Rentenversicherung).
The German government states that anyone born before 1953 could retire at the age of 63 without any deductions after a 45-year insurance period.
However, in reality the name is misleading because the age at which people can retire is being pushed back in line with their year of birth. In practice it is now only available at age 64.5 (and soon to be 65).
Alternatively, people can retire at 63 after 35 years of pension contributions, but this is a different pension and comes with a permanent deduction of 0.3 percent for every month they retire before the applicable retirement age. The maximum deduction is 14.4 percent.
What is the government planning?
The coalition government, made up of the conservative Union (CDU/CSU) and centre left Social Democrat (SPD) parties, is putting together legislation following recommendations from an expert commission unveiled in June.
Getting rid of the Rente mit 63 is one of the most significant and contentious parts of the proposed reform.
The commission is also proposing to raise the minimum age for the separate pension available after 35 years of insurance (with deductions) from 63 to 64.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz said "all elements of this reform package... must now be implemented swiftly".
Merz said the proposals aim to meet "two goals: securing pensions, and ensuring that burdens are distributed fairly across all segments of society and across all generations".
READ ALSO: What Germany's planned pension reform means for you
How many people benefit from early retirement without a reduction?
The early retirement pension without reductions is popular, with around one in three old-age pensioners taking advantage of it. Figures show between 250,000 and 280,000 people per year opt for it.
The scheme was initially intended as a concession for people in physically demanding jobs such as bricklayers, tilers and care workers.
However, figures show that it is primarily people with ‘stable employment histories’ who benefit from it. Men, people on higher incomes and, generally speaking, those in good health benefit from it more often than average, broadcaster BR24 reports.
How much does the early pension without deductions cost?
Those who retire early pay into the pension scheme for a shorter period and generally receive payments for a longer time – that's what makes it so expensive to the state, and why it's in the firing line.
Figures from BR24, citing the German Pension Insurance Fund, say the Rente mit 63 results in additional costs of around €3.5 billion each year.
How much could be saved?
Germany could save roughly €9.5 billion per pension cohort if the Rente mit 63 were abolished, according to a recent DIW Berlin study.
As people would retire later, a further 125,000 full-time workers could potentially remain in employment longer.
Experts say these benefits would lead to a reduction in pension contributions for workers.

items.title: What are the rules on dashcams and doorbell cameras in Germany?
items.summary: Germans are famously protective of their privacy. With dashcams, doorbell cameras and personal assistants like Alexa becoming increasingly common, we look at what you need to know about using these devices in public.
items.body_text:
If you’ve been invited into a German home, you might be surprised to see your hosts locking a personal assistant like Alexa or Siri away in a cupboard.
This isn’t just a quirky habit, it’s a reflection of how seriously privacy is taken here. For many Germans, the idea of a device listening in, even passively, is enough to warrant caution – especially when guests are present.
Strict data protection rules apply in Germany around devices that record images or sound, especially when used in public areas or on people outside of your immediate family.
Below, we explain the rules around using doorbell cameras, dashcams, personal assistants and filming or recording people with mobile phones.
Central to all these devices is the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), which governs how personal data – including images, voices and licence plates – can be processed in Germany.
GDPR is designed to ensure that individuals have rights over their personal data, and that only the minimum necessary data may be collected or stored. Practically speaking in most cases, it means you need others' permission to record their image or voice.
Dashcams
Dashcams – those small cameras mounted on the dashboard or windscreen of your car – are increasingly popular for recording traffic conditions or providing evidence after an accident, but their use in Germany is surrounded by strict legal limits and a strong emphasis on privacy.
Here, you cannot film anyone against their will and it’s strictly forbidden to share recordings of other people or their licence plates online without their explicit permission.
This means that setting your dashcam to record continuously as you drive is not allowed and typically breaches GDPR, unless you can prove you have a compelling reason to do so. Dashcams should only be activated briefly and in direct response to specific events, such as an accident or a sudden incident on the road.
If you use a dashcam in a way that doesn’t comply with these regulations, you could face a hefty fine.
It’s also important to note that only the police are allowed to use video recordings for criminal prosecution – and even then, only under very limited circumstances – which means that anyone offering the police filmed evidence of traffic offences may find themselves facing a fine rather than being met with praise.
In rare cases, courts may accept dashcam recordings as evidence in accident liability proceedings, but this is the exception rather than the rule. According to the experts at ADAC, German courts generally prefer short, event-related recordings, which are far more likely to be considered admissible.
READ ALSO: Everything that changes for drivers in Germany in 2026
Doorbell cameras
Doorbell cameras are increasingly common at peoples' homes, offering residents a convenient way to see who’s at the door and also to enhance security.
But strict rules apply to their use, and understanding these is essential for avoiding legal trouble.
In Germany, you are only permitted to use security cameras to film your own property. Filming neighbouring properties or public roads is generally off limits, and doing so can lead to legal action or claims for damages.
If your doorbell camera is aimed at a public pathway or a neighbour’s property, you are legally obliged to inform anyone affected by displaying a clear sign.
In addition, doorbell cameras should only transmit images after the doorbell has been pressed, should not store recordings permanently, and should automatically interrupt transmission after a few seconds.
The view should be restricted to what you would see through a traditional door peephole.

items.title: What new EU banking law means for foreigners in Germany
items.summary: If you live in Germany and have an account with a UK, US or other non-EU bank, you may have recently received a message telling you about a new EU directive. Here's what it means for foreigners in Germany.
items.body_text:
Having bank accounts in non-EU countries could be about to get more complicated for German residents, due to the EU's Capital Requirements Directive, Article 21(c).
It's not uncommon for foreigners living in Germany to keep one or more bank accounts in their country of origin – often these were opened when the person was still a resident, and maintained after they moved to Germany.
They can be vital to keep up with financial affairs such as taxes in the home country, and are especially important for pensioners as some pensions cannot be paid into a bank account in another country.
But some changes are on the horizon, due to the implementation of the EU directive.
What does the directive say?
The Capital Requirements Directive (CRD6) will require non-EU banks, financial institutions and other entities who provide 'core banking services' in an EU country to establish an authorised local branch.
Core banking services are defined as taking deposits, providing loans or credit guarantees. Find the full text of the law here
What does it mean for residents in Germany who have accounts in a non-EU country?
If you have an account with a bank in a non-EU country, they will have to either set up a local branch in Germany, or enter into an agreement with a local subsidiary in order to continue providing services to Germany-based clients, unless one of the exemptions applies (more on those below).
In practical terms, this means that residents in Germany who have an account with a bank outside the EU may soon be receiving letters asking them to provide an address in the country where the bank account is based.
Other banks may inform their EU-based clients that they cannot keep their account open.
How is this different to Germany's current law?
The new directive is a standardising law, aimed at ensuring that all EU countries have the same rules when it comes to dealing with non-EU banks or financial organisations.
At present, it is up to individual member states to decide on the rules.
Under current German law, you're allowed to hold a foreign bank account but you must declare any interest or foreign-earned income to the tax office (Finanzamt).
However, some banks do not allow residents who live abroad to hold accounts. Following Brexit, some Brits living in Germany found their UK banks closed their account.
The new EU directive seems to have prompted many banks and financial institutions outside Germany to update or revise their policies when it comes to dealing with customers in the EU.
READ ALSO: 'Avoid German banks' - Your best tips for banking in Germany
When does it come into force?
The directive was passed in July 2024, and EU member states were then given an implementation period.
Countries were required to add the directive into their national laws by January 10th, 2026, with a start date of January 11th, 2027 at the latest.
Germany has opted for the January 11th, 2027 start date.
However, a 'grandfathering' clause came into effect on July 11th, 2026 which means that contracts signed before this date are exempt from some aspects of the new law.
The combination of the July date and the January 11th full start date means that banks are now starting to notify customers about the changes.
Are there exemptions?
Yes, there are two important exemptions to the new directive.
The first is 'reverse solicitation'. The restrictions will not apply where an EU client has approached the non-EU bank/lender at their "own exclusive initiative".
The second is the grandfather clause mentioned above – that a contract entered signed before July 11th 2026 should not be covered by the new legislation.
That should give non-EU banks ample cover to continue dealing with EU-based clients. However, it may be that some banks either take a conservative approach to interpreting the legislation, or simply decide that it is too complicated to continue to deal with clients in the EU.

Acting Head of the National Disaster Mitigation Agency’s (BNPB) Center for Disaster Data, Information, and Communication Berton SP Panjaitan said Sunday that the ship had arrived at Reo Port in Manggarai District after sailing from Surabaya.
“As of Saturday (August 22), the ship had treated 21 patients, including those requiring fracture surgery, laceration treatment, outpatient care, and three inpatients,” he said.
According to Panjaitan, KRI Dr. Soeharso serves as a hospital support ship equipped with comprehensive medical facilities, including an emergency room, intensive care unit, operating theater, clinic, pharmacy, laboratory, and treatment rooms.
Two treatment rooms, each equipped with 20 beds, will also be prepared, with separate facilities for male and female patients.
Panjaitan noted that the 122-meter-long ship is also equipped with a helicopter landing deck to facilitate medical evacuations from remote areas.
In addition to these facilities, the hospital ship carries a joint medical team from the Indonesian Navy and the Ministry of Health.
The medical services include general health checks, wound care, surgery, and emergency treatment. All services are provided free of charge and prioritized based on medical needs.
The government hopes the hospital ship will enable residents in affected areas to receive prompt and appropriate medical treatment.
Previously, the Ministry of Health activated nine Health Emergency Operation Centers (HEOCs) to strengthen coordination, monitor the situation, and ensure that post-earthquake healthcare needs in East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) are promptly addressed.
Health Minister Budi Gunadi Sadikin said on August 18 that the immediate priority was to restore all hospitals in affected districts and cities to full operational capacity, particularly in anticipation of a potential increase in patients in the coming days.
The government is targeting all earthquake-affected Regional General Hospitals (RSUD) in NTT to resume basic services within a week, with a focus on trauma surgery, maternal and child healthcare, and hemodialysis.

items.title: Indonesia tackles drought across 1,229 locations amid strong El Nino
items.summary: The Indonesian Ministry of Public Works is taking measures to address drought at 1,229 locations as of August 21, 2026, ...
items.body_text:
Public Works Minister Dody Hanggodo emphasized that water availability is essential to sustaining development, particularly in the agricultural sector, which depends heavily on reliable water supplies.
“Quality water services are the backbone of economic, social, and environmental development, especially in regions facing limited water resources and the impacts of climate change,” he said in Jakarta on Saturday.
Through its Directorate General of Water Resources, the ministry continues to intensify efforts to mitigate the impacts of drought driven by a strong El Niño across Indonesia.
Ministry data showed that interventions had been completed at 1,072 of the 1,229 locations, while work was still underway at the remaining 157 sites.
The efforts covered 157 agricultural sites, 931 residential areas, and 141 areas vulnerable to land and forest fires. The measures have helped protect approximately 41,252 hectares of rice fields and secure access to clean water for 616,033 residents.
In the agricultural sector, various measures have been implemented to maintain rice production, including pumping water from rivers, dredging irrigation channels, constructing emergency canals, and optimizing water distribution networks. Of the 157 agricultural sites targeted, interventions had been completed at 124 locations.
Meanwhile, in residential areas, the ministry is prioritizing basic community needs by distributing clean water. Of the 931 targeted locations, work had been completed at 811.
Efforts are also underway to address land and forest fire risks, with interventions completed at 137 of the 141 targeted sites through hotspot suppression and other fire prevention measures.
Through these measures, the Ministry of Public Works continues to mobilize available resources and infrastructure to mitigate the impacts of drought, secure public water supplies, and protect agricultural land to sustain food production.
The efforts are in line with the ministry’s PU 608 Main Objective, which guides infrastructure development toward delivering tangible benefits to the public and supporting economic growth.

items.title: Pelaku Industri Soroti Keseimbangan Regulasi dan Inovasi dalam Perkembangan Kripto
items.summary: Tokenisasi dinilai menjadi jembatan antara aset tradisional dan ekosistem on-chain, sementara regulasi tetap dibutuhkan.
items.body_text:
Pelaku Industri Soroti Keseimbangan Regulasi dan Inovasi dalam Perkembangan Kripto
Tokenisasi dinilai menjadi jembatan antara aset tradisional dan ekosistem on-chain, sementara regulasi tetap dibutuhkan.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Industri kripto memasuki fase baru dengan semakin terhubungnya institusi keuangan tradisional dan teknologi blockchain.
- Tokenisasi dinilai menjadi jembatan antara aset tradisional dan ekosistem on-chain, sementara regulasi tetap dibutuhkan.
- Likuiditas, UX, infrastruktur, stablecoin, dan edukasi menjadi perhatian dalam memperluas akses terhadap aset digital.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA - Industri kripto memasuki fase baru ketika semakin banyak institusi keuangan tradisional mulai terkoneksi dengan aset digital dan teknologi blockchain.
Perkembangan ini menjadi peluang besar, namun sekaligus menjadi tantangan dalam membawa kripto semakin dekat dengan sistem keuangan mainstream tanpa menghilangkan kecepatan inovasi dan prinsip keterbukaan.
CEO Indodax, William Sutanto, melihat tokenisasi menjadi salah satu jembatan paling konkret antara kedua dunia tersebut.
Baca juga: Orang Kaya Mulai Kurangi Properti, Saham dan Kripto Dinilai Lebih Menarik
Ia menyebut, aset finansial tradisional kini semakin memungkinkan untuk direpresentasikan secara on-chain, membuka peluang bagi investor kripto maupun institusi perbankan saat ini untuk berinteraksi serta bertransaksi dalam ekosistem yang sama.
“Ketika aset tradisional mulai masuk ke blockchain, batas antara traditional finance dan kripto menjadi semakin tipis. Ini membuka peluang yang besar, tetapi juga membutuhkan kepercayaan, regulasi, dan infrastruktur yang mampu menghubungkan kedua ekosistem tersebut,” ujar William pada acara Coinfest Asia 2026 dikutip Minggu (23/8/2026).
Menurutnya, perubahan tersebut juga terlihat dari profil investor yang semakin matang.
Jika sebelumnya kripto banyak diasosiasikan dengan spekulasi dan pergerakan pasar jangka pendek, kini semakin banyak investor dengan pemahaman yang lebih baik, serta banyak institusi melihatnya sebagai bagian dari pilihan investasi yang lebih luas.
Di tengah meningkatnya keterlibatan institusi, William juga menilai regulasi tetap menjadi elemen fundamental bagi perlindungan konsumen dan kepercayaan pasar.
William juga melihat bahwa laju perkembangan industri kripto berlangsung lebih cepat dibandingkan sistem keuangan tradisional.
“Kripto dan blockchain pada dasarnya merupakan playground yang besar bagi inovasi di sektor finansial. Ruang inilah yang menjadi salah satu alasan industri ini bisa berkembang begitu cepat. Karena itu, penting untuk menjaga keseimbangan agar regulasi tetap memberikan perlindungan, sekaligus memberi ruang bagi pengembangan produk dan layanan baru secara terarah,” jelasnya.
Keseimbangan tersebut juga menjadi penting bagi daya saing pelaku industri lokal. William melihat platform domestik perlu tetap memiliki ruang untuk mengembangkan produk yang relevan, terutama ketika berhadapan dengan platform offshore yang memiliki fleksibilitas lebih besar dalam menghadirkan inovasi baru.
Selain regulasi, William menilai likuiditas juga selalu menjadi dasar penting bagi pertumbuhan pasar domestik.
Menurutnya, salah satu tugas utama industri adalah membuat perpindahan antara mata uang fiat dan aset kripto semakin mudah, sekaligus membangun infrastruktur dan pengalaman pengguna yang dapat menjangkau masyarakat lebih luas.
Stablecoin juga dinilai akan memainkan peran semakin besar sebagai penghubung antara sistem keuangan konvensional dan ekonomi on-chain, terutama karena memberikan jalur yang lebih familiar bagi pengguna untuk masuk ke ekosistem aset digital.

items.title: Cerita Hanung Bramantyo Pulihkan Trauma Anak Usai Melihat Penganiayaan
items.summary: Tak hanya membawa anak ke psikolog, suami Zaskia Adya Mecca ini juga menunjukkan totalitasnya sebagai orang tua.
items.body_text:
Cerita Hanung Bramantyo Pulihkan Trauma Anak Usai Melihat Penganiayaan
Tak hanya membawa anak ke psikolog, suami Zaskia Adya Mecca ini juga menunjukkan totalitasnya sebagai orang tua.
Ringkasan Berita:
- Hanung Bramantyo bawa sang putri, Kala Madali, ke psikolog untuk atasi trauma pascainsiden penganiayaan karyawannya.
- Hanung rela tinggalkan jadwal syuting film demi mendampingi Kala yang dipanggil jadi saksi di Pengadilan Militer.
- Sebelum sepakat berdamai, Hanung pastikan kondisi mental sang anak pulih dan tidak lagi menyimpan dendam.
TRIBUNNEWS.COM, JAKARTA - Sutradara Hanung Bramantyo mengakui putrinya Kala Madali Bramantyo sempat mengalami trauma mendalam akibat peristiwa dugaan penganiayaan yang menimpa karyawannya akhir tahun lalu.
Untuk memulihkan kondisi mental sang anak, Hanung bahkan membawanya melakukan konseling ke psikolog.
"Pada saat kejadian Kala trauma udah pasti, ketakutan. Saya sadar bahwa kondisi psikologis itu butuh bantuan dari pihak luar. Jadi kita konseling kepada psikolog gitu," kata Hanung saat ditemui di kawasan Kemang, Jakarta Selatan, Sabtu (22/8/2026).
Baca juga: Karakter Oki & Nirmala Resmi Diangkat Jadi Film, Sutradaranya Hanung Bramantyo
Tak hanya membawa ke psikolog, suami Zaskia Adya Mecca ini juga menunjukkan totalitasnya sebagai orang tua.
Hanung juga sempat meninggalkan aktivitas dan pekerjaan syuting filmnya demi hadir langsung mendampingi sang putri yang harus berhadapan dengan proses hukum dan dipanggil menjadi saksi.
Hanung tak menampik momen persidangan menjadi pengalaman yang sangat berat dan menegangkan, tidak hanya bagi anaknya tetapi juga bagi dirinya sendiri.
"Itu yang momen buat saya sangat berat sekali waktu itu karena saya harus meninggalkan semua pekerjaan saya, ada syuting saya tinggalkan apa segala macam untuk menemani anak ya gitu kan, takutnya nanti terjadi apa-apa," tuturnya.
Pastikan Sang Anak Tak Lagi Dendam Sebelum Berdamai
Sebelum Zaskia melangkah ke proses mediasi resmi, Hanung terlebih dahulu memastikan kondisi psikologis dan perasaan Kala.
Ia ingin memastikan sang buah hati benar-benar telah siap serta lega secara emosional tanpa menyimpan rasa dendam sebelum kesepakatan damai dibuat.
"Dia menganggap ini semuanya adalah bagian dari proses media ya kan, dan kemudian ya sudah apa yang bisa kita lakukan adalah memaafkan, pemaafan," ujar Hanung.
"Toh itu juga dia melakukan itu memang karena terdorong situasi yang memang nggak baik dan saya berharap itu kita mengambil hikmahnya. Itu aja sih," pungkasnya.
Kronologi Kejadian
Insiden penganiayaan terhadap Faisal Henry—sopir sekaligus penjaga rumah keluarga Hanung terjadi di kawasan Jalan Ampera Raya, Jakarta Selatan, pada akhir September 2025 lalu.
Peristiwa berawal saat korban yang sedang mengantar anak Zaskia Adya Mecca hampir ditabrak oleh oknum anggota TNI berinisial Praka NC yang berkendara melawan arus.
Klakson peringatan yang ditiupkan korban justru memicu emosi pelaku hingga terjadi pemukulan.

items.title: The women of Cinemalaya
items.summary: Many have noted the excellent films in Cinemalaya 22, but what’s truly worth noting are the outstanding performances by women
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- Ruby Ruiz and Marietta 'Pokwang' Subong shared the Best Actress award, with both actresses reflecting on their roles and the challenges faced by their characters.
- The festival showcased strong performances by women, with various actresses discussing their roles and the emotional preparation required for their characters.
“I have watched only two full-length films in competition at the Cinemalaya film festival. Mag-iina and A.ni.mal. But I pity the jury. Because the actors are so good! How will you rate them? Halimaw! Lamon! (Powerhouse performances!)”
Thus wrote multi-awarded film director Dwein Baltazar in Filipino on her social media account on August 12.
Mag-iina got the lion’s share of the Cinemalaya awards, including this year’s best film and outstanding direction, screenplay, production design, and musical score. A.ni.mal, on the other hand, received the Balanghai trophy for editing and supporting actress.
So many people who have been part of the independent film festival for many years as organizers, cast, and crew — and even the audience — have noted how excellent the films in this batch are.
But what’s truly worth noting are the outstanding performances by women.
Ruby Ruiz, Status: Rejected
Ruby Ruiz depicted the role of a lonely 69-year-old woman with an American dream in Status: Rejected.
“Not much preparation needed for this role because Biring is pretty much like Ruby,” quipped the veteran actress, who shared the Cinemalaya 22 Best Actress honors with Marietta “Pokwang” Subong.
“At 65, I realized that I yearn for more attention and affection from my children. When you feel that your relevance is diminishing, you amplify that to loneliness. I go through that now and am trying to cope with it.”
This is her fourth Cinemalaya win, having won Best Actress for Iska in 2019, and Best Supporting Actress for Ekstra in 2013 and Ginhawa in 2022.
“It was so much fun, and easy because [my co-actors were] all good, especially Alessandra de Rossi,” she replied. The other cast members are Beverly Salviejo and Yani Villarosa.
Marietta ‘Pokwang’ Subong, 2 Valid IDs
Marietta “Pokwang” Subong starred in 2 Valid IDs as Sylvia, a woman desperate to obtain two identification cards to be able to claim a relative’s substantial remittance from overseas for her ailing husband Ramon (Joey Marquez).
Pokwang, who shared Best Actress with Ruby Ruiz, dedicated her award to all the Sylvias out there.
“Sa lahat ng pinagdadanasan po ng mga Pilipino. ‘Wag kayong mawalan ng pag-asa. Laban lang!” Pokwang said during her acceptance speech.
(To all Filipinos who are going through hardships, never lose hope. Just keep fighting!)
Pokwang won her first Cinemalaya award 10 years ago for her performance in Mercury is Mine.
“Alam ko mahirap ang buhay ngayon. Tipid-tipid. Pero andiyan kayo, sumusuporta. Pinatunayan ’nyong kaya natin ito. Bangon industriya. Kaya natin. Kaya ng Pilipino,” she said
(I know times are really hard. We’re all trying to make ends meet. But here you are, supporting us by watching our movie. You proved that we can ride this out. Let’s uplift the film industry. We can do it. We, Filipinos, can do this.)
Jackie Lou Blanco, Mag-iina
Jackie Lou Blanco, depicted the complicated and very difficult role of the matriarch of three generations of women “bound by grief, madness, and a dark family secret,” in the psychological horror film Mag-iina.
Jackie Lou said Mag-iina came at the most demanding time of her career. Soon after finishing Anthropology for Barefoot Theatre Collaborative and the rerun of The Foxtrot, she multi-tasked a GMA teleserye and rehearsals for Virgin LabFest’s Lualhati while shooting Mag-iina.

items.title: [Tech Thoughts] A Rappler conversation about creativity and AI assistance
items.summary: To what extent should one tag AI assistance they accept in creative work? We tackle the topic on Rappler's Everyday Tech chat channel.
items.body_text:
AT A GLANCE
- The Rappler Communities app's Everyday Tech channel discussed the intersection of creativity and AI, highlighting Apple's plan to label AI-generated music and the introduction of AI Transparency Tags.
- The conversation explored the need for disclosure in various creative pursuits involving AI, suggesting a tiered approach to distinguish between AI as a tool and AI taking over the creative process.
Over on the Rappler Communities app’s Everyday Tech channel, our Friday morning conversation this week turned to a discussion about creativity and AI assistance.
Our discussion started off with a report that Apple Music was planning to add labels to songs made with AI. According to Billboard, Apple said any song tagged as being “materially generated using AI” by content providers, such as record labels and distributors, will have a visible label on the service.
Apple’s action follows a move to institute AI Transparency Tags, which requires content providers to disclose when and where AI is used in a “material” way — including artwork, track, composition, and music video composition.
Earlier in August, Spotify also introduced AI labels to its tracks — specifically an AI Persona badge on specific artists’ profiles. Meanwhile, Bandcamp banned AI use on its platform.
The conversation about AI and creativity made its way towards disclosing AI use for other creative pursuits. Gemma Mendoza, Rappler’s head of strategic programs, and I were discussing the sort of sliding scale of creativity and disclosure — between AI as a tool or an enabler.
For instance, does the use of an AI-powered grammar checker require a disclosure? How about using AI to help in formatting presentation slides?
I felt that the disclosure of AI use was important, but that maybe there should be a tiered approach to AI disclosure so as to distinguish between AI as a helper or tool versus AI taking over for the entire creative process.
For instance, Rappler has AI summaries, and for stories I handle or write, I also make sure the summaries are accurate. That said, I don’t treat the AI summary as my own words, even if I did write the story that created the AI summary.
Going back to the discussion of musicmaking, Gemma said that an issue worth discussing was whether an AI user would be shortcutting their way through music creation — or perhaps through other types of creative work.
“I think that at the end of the day — even if you used AI — the question would be similar to when you put your name on something. If it is crap, then you created crap,” she explained.
The conversation lasted about an hour, and there wasn’t anything definitive or life-changing about it, but it made me think more about my own prejudices against AI and using it. I’m still hesitant to use AI as I do prefer doing my own creative work, but it’s those kinds of discussions that broaden our worldviews just a little bit more, making these conversations worthwhile to have.
For those interested in joining a conversation, do download the Rappler app and in the Communities section, join the Everyday Tech chat channel. We have conversations from Monday to Friday at 10 am and 4 pm. We welcome new perspectives or ideas for topics to tackle next, aside from discussing the latest news about technology. – Rappler.com

items.title: Chinese robots beat Usain Bolt’s 100m world record
items.summary: Two Chinese robots at the World Humanoid Robot Games in China eclipse the 9.58-second world record Usain Bolt set at the 2009 World Athletics Championships
items.body_text:
BEIJING, China – A Chinese humanoid robot ran 100 meters in 9.39 seconds in a preliminary heat at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing on Saturday, August 22, faster than the men’s world record held by Jamaican sprinting great Usain Bolt.
Tiangong Ultra, developed by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, won its heat at the opening of the games’ second edition, organizers said.
The robot overtook smartphone maker Honor’s Lightning near the finish after falling behind early in the race. Lightning finished in 9.47 seconds, also faster than the 9.58-second record Bolt set at the 2009 World Athletics Championships in Berlin.
The two robots lacked Bolt’s flair, slamming straight into a thick mat designed to stop them in their tracks, with Tiangong stumbling wildly into the sidelines, forcing onlookers to move out of the way. Lightning was carried away on a stretcher after collapsing to the ground.
The results nevertheless marked a sharp improvement from last year’s inaugural games, when Tiangong Ultra won the 100 metres in 21.50 seconds. Tiangong also won the world’s first humanoid robot half-marathon, held in Beijing last year.
Earlier on Saturday, Chinese state media reported that Lightning had run 100 metres in 9.32 seconds in a preparatory test, reaching a peak speed of 14.5 meters per second.
Lightning won this year’s humanoid half-marathon in 50 minutes and 26 seconds, faster than the pace of the elite men’s human world record.
Lightning stood 169 cm tall and had 95-cm legs during the half-marathon. Its researchers later lengthened its legs by 10 cm, to 1.05 meters, ahead of the games, according to broadcaster CCTV.
The 100 meters is among 51 events at the games, which include football, dancing, and industrial-task contests.
China sees humanoid robots as strategic industry
China has promoted humanoid robots as a strategic emerging industry, with policymakers and companies betting that advances in AI and hardware will accelerate their use in manufacturing, logistics, and consumer applications.
Investor enthusiasm for the sector was on display earlier this week when shares in Unitree 688836.SS, China’s best-known humanoid robot maker, jumped more than five fold in its Shanghai trading debut on Wednesday, giving the company a market value of about $50 billion.
This year’s games have drawn 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries and six continents, up from 280 teams at the inaugural event.
The games, held at Beijing’s National Speed Skating Oval, run through Wednesday, August 26. – Rappler.com

items.title: AFP rejects China’s ‘deceptive’ narratives on Ayungin Shoal, BRP Sierra Madre
items.summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) pushed back against the Chinese Embassy in Manila accusing Beijing of attempting to "rewrite history" regarding the presence of the BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal.
items.body_text:
AFP rejects China’s ‘deceptive’ narratives on Ayungin Shoal, BRP Sierra Madre
MANILA, Philippines — The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) pushed back against the Chinese Embassy in Manila accusing Beijing of attempting to "rewrite history" regarding the presence of the BRP Sierra Madre at Ayungin Shoal.
In a statement on Saturday, August 22, AFP spokesperson for the West Philippine Sea (WPS), retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, firmly rejected China’s claims about supposed past agreements to remove the grounded naval vessel. He also called out the Chinese Communist Party's (CCP) "track record of deceptive narratives" regarding Philippine waters.
"The Chinese Communist Party speaks of 'promises' and 'demands,' yet it very easily forgets its own track record of deceptive narratives in our waters," Trinidad said.
Trinidad recalled Beijing's 1995 occupation of Panganiban Reef (Mischief Reef), a feature located well within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone (EEZ).
He pointed out that China’s foreign ministry initially assured Manila and the international community that the small wooden structures built there were merely temporary "shelters for local fishermen" with no military intent.
"Today, those 'shelters' have been transformed into a fortified, 550-hectare military airbase complete with a 3,000-meter runway, missile emplacements, radar domes, and naval berths," Trinidad said.
"Mischief Reef stands as a permanent, concrete monument to their deceptive strategy in the West Philippine Sea,” he added.
In contrast to China's illegal land reclamation activities, Trinidad maintained that the BRP Sierra Madre's stationing at Ayungin Shoal represents a lawful and permanent sovereign deployment on a feature over which the Philippines exercises sovereign rights and jurisdiction.
He cited the landmark 2016 Arbitral Tribunal ruling, which explicitly declared Ayungin Shoal a low-tide elevation within the Philippine EEZ and invalidated China's expansive maritime claims as having no legal basis.
"No binding commitment was made to remove the BRP Sierra Madre from Ayungin Shoal," Trinidad said.
Chinese Embassy vs Tarriela
On Sunday, August 24, the Chinese Embassy in Manila responded to a post by Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela.
According to the Chinese Embassy, the Philippines deliberately ran the World War II-era BRP Sierra Madre aground at Ayungin Shoal in May 1999 under the pretext of conducting emergency repairs due to leaks.
The embassy said Beijing immediately protested and demanded the vessel's removal, alleging that Philippine officials had repeatedly promised to tow the ship away.
Since the 2016 ruling, China has continued to insist on the legality of its nine-dash line, despite the Arbitral Tribunal's ruling that the claim has no legal basis under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
This has led to repeated confrontations between Chinese coast guard vessels and maritime militia and the Philippine Coast Guard and Filipino fishermen.

items.title: Philippines nears entry in Tokyo Convention on education
items.summary: The Philippines moves closer to joining the Tokyo Convention on the recognition of higher education qualifications, Commission on Higher Education Chairperson Shirley Agrupis said.
items.body_text:
Philippines nears entry in Tokyo Convention on education
MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines moves closer to joining the Tokyo Convention on the recognition of higher education qualifications, Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Chairperson Shirley Agrupis said.
CHED said the proposed accession received positive reception during the Senate committee on foreign relations hearing on Aug. 20, with discussions highlighting its benefits for Filipino students and graduates.
“Accession to the convention can support greater student and academic mobility, further studies, recognition of partial studies, microcredentials and lifelong learning, while strengthening cooperation among higher education systems across the Asia-Pacific,” CHED said.
President Marcos signed the Instrument of Accession on Oct. 10, 2025.
CHED added that with Senate concurrence, the Philippines would become the first ASEAN country to become a State Party to the Tokyo Convention.
The commission said it continues to support the country’s accession as part of efforts to strengthen the international standing of Philippine higher education and create more opportunities for Filipino learners and graduates across borders.

items.title: Philippines-Japan defense agreement takes effect
items.summary: Bilateral defense relations between the Philippines and Japan reached a new milestone yesterday with the entry into force of the Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement.
items.body_text:
Philippines-Japan defense agreement takes effect
MANILA, Philippines — Bilateral defense relations between the Philippines and Japan reached a new milestone yesterday with the entry into force of the Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement (ACSA).
The main agreement signed in January this year has matured into a deal that will further bolster the partnership of the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Japan Self Defense Force.
It establishes a framework such as the settlement procedures for the reciprocal provision of supplies and services between the two allied military forces.
Department of National Defense spokesman Arsenio Andolong said the DND welcomes the Aug. 22 entry into force of the ACSA.
Andolong said the framework “further strengthens our operational cooperation through the efficient and coordinated provision of supplies and services between the Armed Forces of the Philippines and the Self-Defense Forces of Japan, which will greatly impact our bilateral activities, including exercises and humanitarian assistance and disaster response.”
“This agreement also demonstrates the practical application of our comprehensive strategic partnership with Japan, characterized by mutual trust and our aspiration for a free and open Indo-Pacific region,” he said.
Last month, Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi held an Exchange of Diplomatic Notes for the entry into force of the ACSA during the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.
Bilateral relations between the Philippines and Japan have seen significant developments recently, particularly on defense cooperation, following the signing of the Reciprocal Access Agreement in 2024.

items.title: Woman defecates in her seat on AirAsia flight with toilet just 5 meters away
items.summary: AirAsia said it disinfected the cabin of a Shanghai-bound flight after a woman defecated in her seat during the descent, leaving passengers with the smell for the last 40 minutes of the overnight service.
items.body_text:
Flight AK1516 left Kota Kinabalu at about 10:30 p.m. on Aug. 18 and was scheduled into Shanghai's Pudong International Airport around 3 a.m. the next morning.
Passengers began posting accounts of the flight on Chinese social media on Aug. 19, Shanghai's Xinmin Evening News reported.
A passenger surnamed Zhuo, seated with his wife across the aisle in the same row, told Jimu News the smell reached them 40 to 50 minutes before touchdown and woke passengers in the rows ahead and behind.
The woman appeared to be in her 40s, he said, and sat in a middle seat between two boys of around 10.
"It was just before 2 a.m. and we were all asleep," he said. "She hurried toward the toilet carrying a bag, and then a strange smell came out."
Passengers first assumed someone had vomited. Zhuo's wife suspected one of the boys, but both were asleep.
The cabin understood what had happened only after a passenger in the row ahead turned around and pointed out waste on the floor.
The woman had used a plastic bag, Zhuo said, but the contents spilled onto the aisle carpet and her seat.
Confronted by angry passengers, she said she was unwell and asked who never gets sick.
The toilet was about five meters behind them and had not been closed, he said, adding that they were in row 26 on an aircraft with roughly 30 rows.
A crew member wiped the area with tissues and sprayed air freshener, but the smell persisted.
He said the air conditioning was off because the aircraft was preparing to land, and described the following 40 minutes as excruciating. Passengers crowded into the aisle near the door once the plane was on the ground and taxiing.
AirAsia said in a statement issued in Shanghai on Aug. 21 that cabin crew found an abnormal hygiene situation in the aisle as the aircraft prepared to land, and that they prioritized a safe landing while carrying out a basic cleanup with gloves and towels, The Paper reported.
The captain and ground team were notified on landing, and cleaners disinfected the area after all passengers had disembarked, the airline said. Crew operating the return flight were briefed on the incident and the condition of the cabin.
Frank Tang Ting, AirAsia's general manager for China, said the company recognized the cabin crew's professionalism, composure and speed in handling the situation, and that passenger safety and well-being were central to its work. He thanked passengers for their understanding.

items.title: Singaporean jailed in Malaysia after ride-hailing driver posted video of him insulting Islam
items.summary: A Singaporean security guard has been jailed for 14 days and fined RM7,000 ($1,730) by a Malaysian court after pleading guilty to insulting Islam during a ride-hailing trip in Johor Bahru.
items.body_text:
Mohamed Anim Atam, 56, who was unrepresented, entered his plea on Aug. 21 before Magistrate A. Shaarmini at the Johor Bahru Magistrates' Court, Bernama reported.
The court ordered his jail term to run from Aug. 18, the day he was arrested, and set a default sentence of three months in prison should he fail to pay the fine.
The charge, framed under Section 298 of Malaysia's Penal Code, accused him of deliberately uttering words insulting Islam with the intention of wounding another person's religious feelings, The Star reported.
The provision carries up to one year in prison, a fine, or both.
The offence took place at about 5 p.m. on July 30, while Mohamed Anim was riding as a passenger from Jalan Tun Razak to Jalan Meldrum in central Johor Bahru.
He described the contents of the Quran as lacking compassion and concerned only with killing, Malay Mail reported, citing the facts of the case presented in court.
The driver, Muhamad Danial Haikal Nadzahakim, 29, overheard the remarks and recorded the conversation, then uploaded a two-minute, 20-second clip to social media.
In the recording, the driver identifies himself as a Muslim, disputes the passenger's characterization of the faith and at one point threatens to put him out of the car, according to Mothership.
The passenger apologizes before leaving the vehicle at the roadside. The video circulated widely and a police report was lodged on July 31.
Mohamed Anim was arrested at about 4:15 p.m. on Aug. 18 at the Sultan Iskandar Building in Bukit Chagar, the customs and immigration complex at the Johor Bahru end of the causeway to Singapore.
Officers from the Criminal Investigation Division of the Johor Bahru South district police headquarters made the arrest with assistance from Singapore police and seized a mobile phone to aid the investigation.
Police said that Singapore authorities handed the man to the Royal Malaysia Police that day, AsiaOne reported.
Seeking leniency, Mohamed Anim told the court he suffered from high blood pressure and was in the middle of divorce proceedings that required him to appear before the Syariah Court in Singapore.

items.title: US judge strikes down policy suspending immigrant visa processing for 75 nations
items.summary: A U.S. judge on Friday struck down, opens new tab a Trump administration policy suspending the issuance of immigrant visas to ​applicants from 75 countries, saying that the policy exceeded Secretary of ‌State Marco Rubio's statutory authority.
items.body_text:
U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas in Manhattan said the policy that the State Department announced in January was "patently unlawful" and ran afoul of federal immigration law, which explicitly stripped the secretary of state of authority over consular officers' processing of immigrant visas.
"The Policy, which categorically prohibits the issuance of immigrant visas based upon the nationality of the applicant, represents a direct abrogation of this statutory scheme," she wrote.
The State Department's suspension that also took effect in January impacted applicants from Latin American countries including Brazil, Colombia, and Uruguay; Balkan nations such as Bosnia and Albania; South Asian countries Pakistan and Bangladesh; and those from many nations in Africa, the Middle East, and the Caribbean.
The State Department said applicants from those countries were "at a high risk for becoming a public charge and recourse to local, state and federal government resources in the United States." The department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling.
Vargas, an appointee of Democratic former President Joe Biden, issued the ruling in a lawsuit filed by immigrant rights groups Catholic Legal Immigration Network and African Communities Together along with applicants for immigrant visas and U.S. citizens who are sponsoring family members from the designated countries for immigrant visas.
President Donald Trump has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown that he says is aimed at improving domestic security.
Rights groups say the crackdown has violated free speech and due process rights and has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

items.title: Bombings and arson continue in South
items.summary: There were 51 violent incidents in the three southernmost border provinces on Saturday night, almost half of them occurring in Narathiwat.
items.body_text:
There were 51 violent incidents in the three southernmost border provinces on Saturday night, almost half of them occurring in Narathiwat.
As of midnight, the southern command of the Internal Security Operations Command reported 51 violent incidents in Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala provinces. Most involved arson, along with bomb explosions, public shootings, property destruction and government vehicle theft.
There were 22 attacks in Narathiwat - in Chanae district (4 incidents), Sri Sakhon (1), Waeng (1), Bacho (3), Muang (1), Cho Airong (1), Rangae (5), Sungai Kolok (1), Tak Bai (2), Yi-ngo (1), Rueso (1) and Sungai Padi (1).
They included bombings, public shootings, state vehicle theft and the torching of buildings, power poles and a backhoe. Two women, aged 45 and 46 years, were injured when a bomb detonated on Ban Tham Niap Road in tambon Lamphu of Muang district, Narathiwat.
One woman suffered ruptures in her chest and left arm, the other a severe wound to her left thigh.
The tambon Bo Ngo administration organisation office in Rangae district was torched. A state-owned pickup truck was stolen from there and was later found burnt-out.
In Pattani, there were 11 violent incidents - in Yarang district (3), Yaring (2), Nong Chik (3), Sai Buri (1), Thung Yang Daeng (1) and Khok Pho (1). There were no injuries.
In Yaring, a 7-Eleven convenience store was bombed. Suspicious objects were also left there by the attackers, who fired gunshots skywards and set fire to tyres. In Sai Buri, a new municipal office in tambon Taluban of Sai Buri district, Pattani, was set ablaze.
In Yala 18 violent incidents were reported - including 8 in Than To district, 6 in Bannang Sata and 2 in Raman. There were no injuries. Most involved attackers burning tyres, surveillance cameras, mobile phone cellular towers and state vehicles. Spikes were also scattered on main roads.
Security officials advise people not to touch any suspicious objects they come across, and to immediately report them.
The Internal Security Operations Command condemned the incidents, saying they did not demonstrate courage, only an intention to hurt people and instill fear.

items.title: Twenty-two crew missing after Singapore-bound bulk carrier sinks off eastern India
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Aug 23 — Rescuers searched today for 22 people missing after a merchant vessel sank off India’s e...
items.body_text:
NEW DELHI, Aug 23 — Rescuers searched today for 22 people missing after a merchant vessel sank off India’s eastern coast, the navy said.
The Panama-flagged bulk carrier MV Ocean Winner was headed to Singapore from Paradip port in India’s Odisha state, according to MarineTraffic.
The vessel sent a distress alert about 700 kilometres (435 miles) east of Visakhapatnam, the navy said, prompting a joint rescue operation with the Indian coast guard.
Two of the 24 crew members were rescued, it said, adding that a navy patrol aircraft had been redeployed to surveil the area.
The coast guard also deployed three vessels, Indian broadcaster NDTV reported.
“The aircraft located life rafts in the area”, and coordinated with a nearby vessel, MT Aisopos, to collect two of the crew from liferafts, the navy said.
Twenty crew members were Chinese, three were from Myanmar and one was Bangladeshi, the Press Trust of India news agency reported, citing coast guard sources.
The nationalities of the two rescued crew members were not immediately clear. — AFP

items.title: Bangladesh’s gas crunch cripples industry as factories close and power cuts spread
items.summary: BRAHMANBARIA, Aug 23 — The giant structures of Bangladesh’s Ashuganj fertiliser factory have stood silent fo...
items.body_text:
BRAHMANBARIA, Aug 23 — The giant structures of Bangladesh’s Ashuganj fertiliser factory have stood silent for more than a year, as a natural gas crisis shuts industries, triggers power cuts and sparks protests over fuel shortages.
Machinery once ran round the clock, using natural gas to produce urea that farmers depended on to grow crops for the country’s 170 million people.
Now the state-owned factory, which once employed more than 1,200 people and produced more than 1,000 tonnes of fertiliser a day, is a rusting shell.
Ashuganj closed in March 2025, with the country battered by a gas shortage sparked by a plunge in production owing to underinvestment in ageing fields and exploration, while the US-Iran war has choked imports from the Middle East.
“Only the skeleton of the factory remains,” said Md Bazlur Rashid, 59, who spent his entire working life at Ashuganj, built near the eastern Titas gas field. “It has lost its life”.
The factory is one of six major urea fertiliser plants that have been forced to close down or restrict operations because of gas shortages.
Trade union leader Md Abu Kawsar said the shutdowns had cost workers their jobs while threatening an industry linked to food security.
“You cannot simply let these factories sit idle and allow them to deteriorate,” he told AFP. “Reviving them could also help save foreign currency.”
But the consequences of the gas shortage extend far beyond fertiliser production.
Hundreds of factories, including textile plants, are cutting production or shutting.
Bangladesh is the world’s second-largest garment exporter, which accounts for about 80 per cent of the country’s export earnings.
At home, domestic piped gas is often cut.
Power plants turning gas into electricity are struggling to meet demand, creating regular blackouts.
The government issued electricity-saving measures in August, including ordering shopping malls to close an hour earlier.
‘Don’t get a drop’
Electricity generation, industry and captive power plants account for more than three-quarters of Bangladesh’s gas consumption.
Households, which account for just over a tenth of the country’s gas consumption, have also been hit.
“We don’t get a drop of gas overnight,” said housewife Nargis Begum, 50, who lives close to the Ashuganj factory.
“Then sometimes the pressure is too low. We can’t turn on two burners at the same time.”
Many households, particularly in rural areas, have switched to wood-burning stoves, while electricity cuts leave residents without fans in the sweltering humidity.
“There is no let-up in our suffering,” said Begum. “There is no guarantee of electricity. It’s so hot now. Last night, there were three or four outages.”
Gas-powered rickshaw drivers have also blocked roads in protest after hours waiting for fuel.
The shortages are the result of a crisis that has been building for years.
Bangladesh was largely self-sufficient in natural gas in 2018, but production declined as older fields depleted, while demand has risen, with Qatar providing key imports.
Experts say successive governments have failed to invest sufficiently in exploration.
Energy Minister Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku blamed the previous government of Sheikh Hasina, ousted in a 2024 revolution, for failing to drill new wells.
“The previous government stayed away from gas exploration,” he told an energy security conference in Dhaka in July. “Our dependence on imports has brought us to this point.”
‘Turn to renewable’
Imports have also proved vulnerable.
The crisis worsened after the war in the Middle East disrupted liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments, with traffic through the Strait of Hormuz severely curtailed.
Supplies were further hit when a floating storage and regasification unit, which processes imported LNG into gas, halted operations because of a technical problem.
With no quick fix, the government is continuing LNG orders and investing in terminals to expand imports, even as experts call for more domestic exploration.

items.title: Magnitude 5.9 earthquake near Tokyo injures at least 37
items.summary: TOKYO, Aug 23 — A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Tokyo early today, injuring at least 37 people and disrupti...
items.body_text:
TOKYO, Aug 23 — A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Tokyo early today, injuring at least 37 people and disrupting travel in the bustling megacity.
The quake caused violent shaking in the Japanese capital and its surrounding areas, prompting the nation’s warning systems to sound public announcements and sirens in the streets and lighting up smartphones with notices in affected areas.
The quake struck the southern part of the Ibaraki Prefecture near Tokyo at 2am (1700 GMT yesterday), the Japan Meteorological Agency said.
There were no concerns about a tsunami, the agency said, adding that the earthquake’s depth was 68 kilometres (42 miles).
The US Geological Survey estimated the strength at magnitude 5.8.
Japan’s Fire and Disaster Management Agency said that at least 37 people had suffered minor injuries.
The worst case was that of a woman in her 80s in Yokohama, south of Tokyo, who tried to leave her bed after the quake but fell and hurt her hip, according to the local government and media reports.
The late-night quake disrupted regional train services in Tokyo today morning, according to East Japan Railway Company.
A building in Saitama, north of Tokyo, also suffered minor damage, according to the Fire and Disaster Management Agency.
Authorities are investigating if a water main that ruptured in a neighbourhood in the capital was related to the quake, Kyodo News said.
The weather agency warned of an increased risk of landslides in the area as the quake could have loosened soil in the region, which was lashed by torrential downpours yesterday.
The agency also warned of the possibilitiy of strong aftershocks in the days ahead. — AFP

items.title: 'Keep up the spirit': Indonesian teenage 'Superman' joins wildfire fight
items.summary: Fires between January and July burned more than 200,000 hectares of land - an area three times the size of the capital Jakarta, the Indonesian government said this week.
items.body_text:
'Keep up the spirit': Indonesian teenage 'Superman' joins wildfire fight
Fires between January and July burned more than 200,000 hectares of land - an area three times the size of the capital Jakarta, the Indonesian government said this week.
PALANGKARAYA, Central Kalimantan: Dressed as his favourite superhero, Indonesian teenager Rudiyansah walks along a charred landscape, helping douse wildfires that have razed large parts of Borneo island.
The Southeast Asian country has been battling infernos that have left a thick, blanketing smog over parts of the island that Indonesia shares with Malaysia and Brunei.
Rudiyansah's red and blue Superman costume stood out against the stark, scorched landscape surrounding the town of Palangkaraya, where he has joined a local volunteer firefighting group set up by his father to put out smouldering peatland.
The 17-year-old told AFP he has been using his free time after school to help his father douse fires since 2023.
But this year, he decided to don the brightly coloured tights when fighting fires, creating a striking image that has drawn attention to the struggle to contain the blazes.
While Rudiyansah said dressing as the Man of Steel was "just for fun", video of him using a hose to wet foliage has gone viral, garnering millions of views and earning him the title of "forest hero" from the country's forestry minister.
"Honestly, I'm really happy because I can help locals, even though it feels really tiring," Rudiyansah, who like many Indonesians only uses one name, told AFP on Sunday (Aug 23) while still wearing his cape.
He said that he wet his costume slightly before heading into the fields to prevent it from burning, and washed it every night to keep it clean.
“NORMAL KID”
His father, Mulyadi, told AFP the haze from this year's fire season was the worst his volunteer firefighter group had seen since it was established in 2020.
"In the house, he's like a normal kid," he said when asked about his cape-clad son.
"But when he saw me going out, he asked, 'Are you going to put out fires? I'll go with you,'" he said.
The lack of water was the main challenge for firefighters, Mulyadi said, with wells and other water sources drying up during drought.
Fires between January and July burned more than 200,000 hectares of land - an area three times the size of the capital Jakarta, the government said this week.
That is already larger than during previous El Nino seasons - a weather pattern that triggers worldwide changes in winds, atmospheric pressure and rainfall - in 2019 and 2023.
The government has ordered more troop and aircraft deployments to help contain the spread of the blazes and smog, which has reached Malaysia.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that typically brings drought, which increased the risks of wildfires, in Indonesia.
Human-caused climate change can amplify its impacts because a warmer ocean and atmosphere make more energy and moisture available to feed extreme weather events.
Rudiyansah, who dreams of becoming a forest ranger someday, called on firefighters to carry on despite the challenges in putting out the fires.
"To volunteers and firefighters across Indonesia, keep up the spirit in the fight against the flames," he said.

items.title: Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case in local mammal
items.summary: South Australian authorities confirmed the nation's first mammalian detection of the H5N1 virus in a long-nosed fur seal, which was found dead with no signs of injury.
items.body_text:
Australia confirms first H5N1 bird flu case in local mammal
South Australian authorities confirmed the nation's first mammalian detection of the H5N1 virus in a long-nosed fur seal, which was found dead with no signs of injury.
SYDNEY: Australia on Sunday (Aug 23) confirmed its first case of H5N1 bird flu in a mammal, with the deadly virus found in a long-nosed fur seal in South Australia state.
Australia has been grappling with rising cases of the highly pathogenic avian influenza after it landed in the country in June. The country's first mass seabird deaths from the virus occurred this month, marking an escalation of the outbreak that began after the virus was first detected in migratory seabirds before spreading to native species.
South Australian authorities confirmed the nation's first mammalian detection in the seal, found at the coastal town of Beachport, about 310km south of Adelaide, the state capital.
The seal, one of an estimated population of 100,000 in the state's waters, was found dead with no signs of injury, the authorities said.
Its death "does not appear to be associated with other sick or dead marine mammals," federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said in televised remarks. "Once the H5 bird flu is spreading in the natural environment it is not possible to avoid significant losses."
Australia was the last continent to report bird flu, although the virus was detected in late 2025 on the sub-Antarctic territory of Heard Island. More than 13,000 baby seals were killed by the virus on the island, according to local media.
Seals are at high risk of contracting the virus, said South Australia's chief veterinary officer, Skye Fruean, because they live very near wild birds on rocky outcrops on the coast.
"They would be coming across, no doubt, really high levels of the virus in their environment," Fruean said in televised remarks.
H5N1 has not shown up in Australia's poultry or agriculture, according to the federal government, which said on Friday that 297 cases have been confirmed nationwide.

The Panama-flagged bulk carrier MV Ocean Winner was headed to Singapore from Paradip port in India's Odisha state, according to MarineTraffic.
NEW DELHI: Rescuers searched on Sunday (Aug 23) for 22 people missing after a merchant vessel sank off India's eastern coast, the navy said.
The Panama-flagged bulk carrier MV Ocean Winner was headed to Singapore from Paradip port in India's Odisha state, according to MarineTraffic.
The vessel sent a distress alert about 700km east of Visakhapatnam, the navy said, prompting a joint rescue operation with the Indian coast guard.
Two of the 24 crew members were rescued, it said, adding that a navy patrol aircraft had been redeployed to surveil the area.
The coast guard also deployed three vessels, Indian broadcaster NDTV reported.
"The aircraft located life rafts in the area", and coordinated with a nearby vessel, MT Aisopos, to collect two of the crew from liferafts, the navy said.
Twenty crew members were Chinese, three were from Myanmar and one was Bangladeshi, the Press Trust of India news agency reported, citing coast guard sources.
The nationalities of the two rescued crew members were not immediately clear.

items.body_text:
Mystery AI model Ox Alpha draws developers with free access
SAN FRANCISCO - A new artificial intelligence model called Ox Alpha is gaining traction among developers after appearing online for free, even as the identity of its creator remains a mystery.
The model appeared on AI marketplace OpenRouter last week under the label “stealth model”. Ox Alpha offers a roughly 1 million-token context window that can process text, image and video input, according to OpenRouter.
The unusual debut has triggered a guessing game among AI developers over who may be behind the model.
Some online speculation has pointed to China, where companies have recently rolled out increasingly capable models, including Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 and Alibaba Group’s latest Qwen models.
A growing number of companies from ByteDance to Sea and Alibaba have in 2026 launched models without initially claiming credit for those platforms.
By not publicising their origins from the start, tech companies may be aiming to test the waters for new-fangled services and initiatives, affording these projects more freedom to experiment.
Ox Alpha is available free with near-unlimited usage for a week, according to OpenCode, helping fuel a surge in experimentation among developers.
Stripe Chief Executive Officer Patrick Collison described it in a post on X as “very impressive”, while users have shared reviews on YouTube and Reddit. Bloomberg

items.title: France’s Macron hosts Saudi crown prince for visit ranging from e-sports to war in Middle East
items.summary: Several agreements on health, transport and energy will be signed on the second day of the visit on Aug 24.
items.body_text:
France’s Macron hosts Saudi crown prince for visit ranging from e-sports to war in Middle East
- French President Emmanuel Macron hosts Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for a two-day visit, including esports events and discussions on Middle East issues.
- Agreements on health, transport, and energy will be signed, highlighting strong Paris-Riyadh ties; a Saudi-backed esports event is held in Paris for the first time.
- Macron and MBS will chair the Saudi-French strategic partnership council to discuss regional stability, amid ongoing tensions and unresolved issues like Jamal Khashoggi's killing.
AI generated
PARIS - French President Emmanuel Macron welcomes Saudi crown prince and de facto ruler Mohammed bin Salman on Aug 23 for a two-day visit set to range from esports to the war in the Middle East.
Several agreements on health, transport and energy will be signed on the second day of the visit on Aug 24, according to a French presidential official, underlining the strength of the Paris-Riyadh relationship.
But the visit will kick off in a different style on the evening of Aug 23 from 1800 GMT (2am Singapore time on Aug 24) with Macron hosting the Saudi strongman – known as MBS – at the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup hosted by Paris.
The event, which brings together the leading performers in esports ranging from computer games to chess and has been eagerly backed by MBS, is being held outside Saudi Arabia for the first time.
The French presidential official declined to comment on whether the agreements could touch on a vast theme park known as Dragons Ball, backed by a Saudi fund, which is mooted for the Val-d’Oise region outside Paris.
Saudi Arabia is also set to host a string of key global events, notably the Expo 2030 and above all the football World Cup in 2034.
Saudi Arabia, a close US ally which has a history of tensions with Iran, is also closely watching developments in the Islamic republic in the wake of the US-Israeli war.
On the afternoon of Aug 24, MBS and Macron are to chair the first meeting of the Saudi-French strategic partnership council.
Macron and MBS “will discuss key regional issues, in a context calling for close coordination between France and its Gulf partners to foster stability and peace” in the Middle East, according to Macron’s office.
It remains unclear if rights will feature high on the agenda, some eight years after dissident Saudi journalist Jamal Khashoggi was killed and dismembered inside Riyadh’s Istanbul consulate in 2018.
A United Nations investigation described Khashoggi’s death as an “extrajudicial killing for which Saudi Arabia is responsible”.
US intelligence agencies determined that MBS had “approved” the operation that led to Khashoggi’s killing. Riyadh denies this, blaming rogue operatives.
In December 2021, Macron became one of the first Western leaders to meet MBS in Saudi Arabia in the wake of the Khashoggi killing.
The Saudi crown prince has made multiple visits to France since then. AFP

items.title: Mexican governor, indicted by US on cartel charges, requests leave again amid backlash
items.summary: Ruben Rocha’s return was not well received by either the Mexican government or the ruling Morena party.
items.body_text:
Mexican governor, indicted by US on cartel charges, requests leave again amid backlash
- Sinaloa governor Ruben Rocha, indicted by US prosecutors for drug trafficking and cartel ties, requested leave again amid political backlash after returning to office.
- Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Morena party criticised Rocha for putting personal interests above public good.
- US charges allege Rocha aided the Sinaloa Cartel's drug trafficking in exchange for bribes; Rocha calls the case politically motivated against Sheinbaum's movement.
AI generated
MEXICO CITY - Sinaloa governor Ruben Rocha, indicted by US federal prosecutors on drug-trafficking, bribery and cartel-protection charges, again requested a leave of absence from office on Aug 22, days after defiantly reclaiming his post.
Rocha’s return was not well received by either the Mexican government or the ruling Morena party, which accused him of prioritising his personal interests over those of the public.
Earlier on Aug 22, President Claudia Sheinbaum warned on X that “power without principles becomes arrogance,” and “no personal interest can ever be above those of the people or the Nation,” intensifying the political firestorm, without directly naming Rocha.
Echoing her words, Rocha posted a statement on X saying that “Sinaloa, the nation, and the transformation movement are above all else.”
Rocha, 77, a member of Sheinbaum’s Morena party, returned to office on Aug 21 after more than three months on leave following US drug-trafficking charges.
In April, US prosecutors alleged Rocha and nine other current and former officials conspired with a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel known as Los Chapitos, helping it to traffic drugs into the US in exchange for political support and bribes.
Washington’s move marked a rare expansion of anti-cartel action beyond drug bosses to include a sitting senior Mexican politician.
Rocha has described the US case as a politically motivated attack on Sheinbaum’s movement.
Sheinbaum’s government previously said Washington did not provide sufficient evidence to justify Rocha’s arrest or extradition, even as her administration opened its own investigation.
But there were signs that Rocha’s return to power was received coolly by Sheinbaum and Morena, underscoring lingering tensions within the ruling party over the case. REUTERS

items.title: Legislature loses ‘friendship’ travel funds
items.body_text:
- 
            Legislature loses ‘friendship’ travel fundsFAIR? That the budget cuts affected the Legislative Yuan shows that they aimed to rein in government spending and were not targeted at the Executive Yuan, a legislator said
  - By Chen Cheng-yu and Lo Kuo-chia / Staff reporters
 The legislature has suspended funding for overseas visits by lawmakers’ friendship groups after travel budget cuts, prompting mixed responses from the three major parties. The central government’s budget for this fiscal year was delayed for 351 days before the Legislative Yuan finally passed it on Friday last week. As part of across-the-board cuts, the budgets for overseas travel and training at central government agencies and their affiliated bodies were cut by 30 percent, with exceptions for legally mandated spending, Academia Sinica and the National Audit Office. Some agencies were subject to cuts ranging from 10 percent to 70 percent. Lawmakers attend a session at the Legislative Yuan in Taipei on Friday last week.Photo: Fang Pin-chao, Taipei Times In a letter sent to lawmakers, Legislative Yuan Secretary-General Chou Wan-lai (周萬來) said that after the cuts, the legislature’s overseas travel budget was insufficient to subsidize lawmakers’ visits organized by foreign parliamentary friendship groups, once existing expenditures and earmarked funds were taken into account. Under Article 15 of the regulations governing parliamentary friendship groups with foreign legislators and other organizations, subsidies must be covered by the legislature’s budget. The Legislative Yuan has stopped accepting applications for funding for overseas visits by parliamentary friendship groups, effective immediately. “I think the legislature has only itself to blame,” Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) caucus secretary-general Fan Yun (范雲) said yesterday, adding that the cuts ended up affecting the Legislative Yuan itself, leaving lawmakers without subsidies and forcing them to pay out of pocket for overseas parliamentary diplomacy. DPP Legislator Michelle Lin (林楚茵), who also chairs the Taiwan-France Parliamentary Friendship Association and other friendship groups, said that there were 114 parliamentary friendship groups as of the end of June, 78 of which are cross-national groups focused on parliamentary diplomacy. At a time when Taiwan is facing pressure from China, parliamentary exchanges with other democratic legislatures are an important way for the nation to engage internationally, she added. The subsidy for overseas visits by parliamentary friendship groups is about NT$60,000 per person, Lin said. While that amount may cover trips to some Asian countries, an economy-class ticket to Europe could cost more than NT$60,000, she said, adding that there are also accommodation expenses. Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT) Legislator Lee Yen-hsiu (李彥秀) said the cuts apply to the Legislative Yuan, which shows that they were intended to rein in government spending, rather than targeting the Executive Yuan. Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) caucus whip Jacky Chen (陳清龍) said cuts have been made at a certain rate in previous years, adding that the 30 percent cut to overseas travel expenses was the version the three parties agreed upon during negotiations. As DPP caucus whip Tsai Chi-chang (蔡其昌) signed off on the agreement, all government agencies would be able to adjust accordingly, Chen said. TPP Legislator Hung Yu-hsiang (洪毓祥) said parliamentary diplomacy is necessary, and lawmakers should continue traveling overseas to seek international support and deepen ties with democratic partners. However, the importance of parliamentary diplomacy does not mean every expense should be given unlimited leeway, he added. Hung criticized some government officials for taking aimless overseas trips and submitting poorly written reports, only to invoke national security confidentiality as a cover when their conduct was exposed. Such misuse of travel funds was the main reason for the cuts, he said,

items.title: US aircraft transits Strait ahead of Xi-Trump meet
items.body_text:
- 
            US aircraft transits Strait ahead of Xi-Trump meet

 A US Navy P-8A Poseidon aircraft transited the Taiwan Strait in international airspace on Friday, in a move the US 7th Fleet said “demonstrates the US’ commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific.” The Chinese military tracked and monitored the patrol and reconnaissance aircraft throughout the transit, the state-backed Global Times newspaper reported, citing a military source, saying the “situation was under control.” US military ships or aircraft pass through or above the waterway that separates Taiwan from China every few months. items.title: Tainan fire injures 15 and damages 68 homes
items.body_text:
- 
            Tainan fire injures 15 and damages 68 homes
  - By Wang Chieh and Hung Jui-chin / Staff reporters, with CNA
 A fire and subsequent explosion in a residential area in Tainan early yesterday injured 15 people and damaged 68 homes, the Tainan City Fire Bureau said. The bureau said it received a report at 1:12am yesterday that a pile of waste in a vacant lot in Annan District’s (安南) Haidian Road had caught fire and exploded, adding that it dispatched 144 firefighters and 53 firetrucks to battle the blaze and evacuate nearby residents. It took more than four hours to extinguish the fire, it said. Buildings and vehicles damaged by a fire and subsequent explosion in a residential area in Tainan are pictured yesterday.Photo courtesy of the Tainan City Government’s Environmental Protection Bureau The incident damaged 11 privately owned vehicles, as well as eight fire engines, one ambulance and two disaster assessment vehicles, the bureau said. The three homes closest to the blast site sustained the most severe damage, it added. Twelve people and three firefighters were injured, sustaining cuts to the head or other minor injuries, the bureau said, adding that no one was seriously hurt. The Tainan City Government’s air quality and pollutant sampling data showed no abnormalities after the incident. A man surnamed Yang (楊) allegedly managed the land, allowing a Kaohsiung waste operator to illegally dump trash outside its jurisdiction in contravention of the Waste Disposal Act (廢棄物清理法), the bureau said, citing a police investigation. The case has been referred to prosecutors, while the Kaohsiung Environmental Protection Bureau has been notified about conducting a joint investigation, it said. Tainan Mayor Huang Wei-che (黃偉哲), who had been visiting Singapore, flew home after learning of the incident and arrived at the scene last night to assess the damage. The city government would prioritize helping affected residents find temporary accommodation and restore their homes, he said, adding that lawyers would be hired to help them seek compensation and hold those responsible accountable. The city government has activated emergency housing and relief measures for the 11 households that were most severely affected, Huang said. Each household would receive NT$20,000 in emergency assistance, and civil engineers would be brought in to assess the structural safety of the homes to provide a basis for subsequent repairs and compensation claims, he added.
